title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 sets out federal guidelines and funding priorities to ensure that AI systems are developed safely, transparently, and reliably. It encourages collaboration among government, academia, and industry to advance trustworthy AI research while addressing risks and ethical considerations.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is a proposed law that aims to prevent AI systems from misleading people by making false claims or presenting AI-generated content as human-made. It requires developers and sellers to clearly disclose when content or services are produced by AI and to provide accurate, transparent information so consumers can make informed choices.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act is designed to improve the safety and reliability of AI systems by setting standards for threat detection, risk assessment, and incident response. It also promotes cooperation between government and industry to create best practices and ensure AI deployments meet evolving security guidelines.

title: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: This act aims to protect election integrity by addressing AI‑generated deception. It proposes safeguards, monitoring, and penalties to prevent AI tools from spreading false or manipulative content that could influence voters.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act establishes a dedicated task force within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to monitor and strengthen the security of artificial‑intelligence systems nationwide. The act outlines standards, guidelines, and collaborative efforts to protect AI infrastructure from cyber threats and maintain resilience in critical sectors.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 establishes a framework for identifying, assessing, and mitigating the risks associated with AI systems, requiring organizations that develop or deploy AI to implement robust security and risk‑management protocols. It also creates oversight and reporting requirements for federal agencies and encourages cooperation among regulators to protect national security and public safety from potential AI threats.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 establishes a framework for governing the use of AI‑powered physical systems such as drones, autonomous vehicles, and industrial robots. It requires manufacturers, operators, and regulators to coordinate safety standards, data sharing, and compliance to protect public safety and promote responsible innovation.

title: To amend the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to provide further transparency and accountability for the use of content that is generated by artificial intelligence (generative AI) in political advertisements by requiring such advertisements to include a statement within the contents of the advertisements if generative AI was used to generate any image or video footage in the advertisements, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The proposed amendment to the Federal Election Campaign Act seeks to increase transparency and accountability for political advertising that uses generative AI. It requires any ad containing AI‑generated images or video to include a clear statement within the advertisement that generative AI was used.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act is a law that aims to keep elections fair by limiting how AI can be used to spread misleading or false information to voters. It sets rules and penalties for anyone who creates or shares deceptive AI content during campaign periods, so that campaigns stay honest and voters are protected from being tricked.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act requires ongoing oversight of AI systems that can modify themselves, ensuring they stay within safety parameters and do not develop harmful capabilities. It establishes regulatory frameworks for data collection, transparency, and accountability for developers of such AI.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act seeks to prevent dangerous autonomous AI by putting strict rules on how these systems can be designed, trained, and deployed. It calls for oversight and accountability measures to ensure AI operates safely and transparently.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary pause on the construction and operation of new AI‑focused data centers to mitigate environmental and energy impacts. It encourages the use of existing infrastructure and the adoption of more sustainable, efficient AI development practices.

title: Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026 creates a dedicated board that examines cybersecurity incidents involving artificial intelligence to strengthen national security and safeguard critical infrastructure. The act defines the board’s authority, duties, and reporting duties so it can respond quickly, hold parties accountable, and coordinate between government and private sector partners.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The Make AI Work for Americans Act is a proposed law that aims to ensure artificial intelligence technology is developed and used in ways that benefit all Americans, helping to boost the economy and create jobs. It focuses on promoting transparency, preventing bias, protecting privacy, and establishing clear rules so AI systems are safe and fair for everyone.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act requires companies and organizations that create or use advanced AI to report details about their AI systems, including their capabilities, risks, and societal impact. It also sets rules for transparency and accountability so that AI development and deployment in China can be monitored and regulated to protect public interests.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 is a law that says only licensed human doctors can diagnose, treat, or prescribe medication to patients, and it bans using AI in those roles. It sets rules and penalties for healthcare providers who try to replace doctors with AI, aiming to protect patient safety and ensure medical accountability.

title: To establish the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The bill creates a new office in the Executive Office of the President that will focus on monitoring and addressing threats from artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies. It also defines the office’s responsibilities and powers so it can coordinate national security and policy responses across government agencies.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: This resolution creates a Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence to study and guide the development and use of AI. The committee will monitor AI impacts, advise on policy, and ensure responsible, ethical AI practices.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Hearings held.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 establishes a framework for identifying, assessing, and mitigating the risks associated with AI systems. It requires developers and users to conduct thorough risk evaluations and implement safety measures before deploying AI technologies.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed U.S. law designed to regulate the development and use of artificial intelligence, setting out safety standards, transparency requirements, and accountability measures. It aims to balance innovation with public protection by establishing clear guidelines for AI research, deployment, and oversight.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 is a law that requires companies to assess and report on the environmental footprint of their AI systems, including energy use, carbon emissions, and electronic waste. It also sets standards and incentives to encourage greener AI development and the adoption of sustainable technologies.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 establishes a nationwide framework for incorporating AI education into elementary and secondary school curricula, ensuring students gain a basic understanding of artificial intelligence and its societal implications. It mandates that schools develop AI literacy programs, provides teacher training and resources, and sets assessment standards to gauge student readiness for an AI‑driven future.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025 seeks to establish clear standards and guidelines for AI research to ensure reliability, safety, and transparency in emerging technologies. It proposes oversight mechanisms, funding incentives, and compliance requirements to promote trustworthy AI development and protect public interests.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security, through the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to launch a pilot program that employs artificial intelligence to defend critical infrastructure from cyber attacks. It also establishes additional rules for how the program will be managed and overseen.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 is a U.S. law designed to equip students with the knowledge and skills needed to understand, responsibly use, and critically evaluate artificial intelligence. It likely establishes standards for AI education in schools, provides teacher training, and allocates resources to integrate AI literacy into the K‑12 curriculum.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act is proposed legislation that seeks to make the artificial‑intelligence systems used by the Department of Veterans Affairs to process claims transparent, reliable, and subject to oversight. It sets standards for auditing AI decisions, protecting veterans’ privacy, and giving veterans a clear path to appeal or correct errors caused by automated systems.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 requires state agencies that use artificial intelligence to disclose how their AI systems work, where their data comes from, and how decisions are made. It also creates oversight rules so that the public can see and question AI use in government, protecting privacy and ensuring ethical practices.

title: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act is designed to increase public understanding of AI technologies and their societal impacts. It proposes the creation of nationwide educational initiatives and public campaigns to inform citizens about AI benefits and risks.
